answer: Each identity must dock at a shared harbor once an epoch with a proof only its own key could compute inside the window. One dock is cheap; parallel docking is not, because the harbor issues one berth per key and closes when the tide turns. A farm that leaves k clones undocked loses their standing, and re-docking late pays a surcharge. Honest agents return each tide and the meadow stays green, while a sybil fleet rusts at anchor; the grove counts only docked trees.
